notes.pest_disease: Cabbage worms and aphids are primary pests. Row covers during early growth protect against caterpillars. Check under leaves regularly for aphid colonies.
notes.harvest_marker: Harvest outer leaves when 8-12 inches long, leaving the growing center intact for continuous production. Leaves should be deep green and firm, not yellowing.
notes.storage_handling: Store at 0-2 degrees C with high humidity. Kale holds well for 2-3 weeks when properly cooled. Blanch and freeze excess harvest.
notes.rotation_companion: Rotate with legumes or root crops. Avoid planting after other brassicas. Plant dill or celery nearby to attract beneficial insects.
notes.cultivar_recommendation: Red Russian is tender and fast-growing for baby leaf. Lacinato (Dinosaur) has excellent flavor and texture for mature harvest. Winterbor is extremely cold-hardy.
notes.growing_tip: Frost improves sweetness significantly. Kale is one of the most nutrient-dense and cold-tolerant crops. Fall plantings often outperform spring plantings in quality.
notes.irrigation: Moderate, consistent irrigation. Kale tolerates short dry spells better than lettuce but benefits from regular moisture during establishment.
notes.nursery_specific: Start 4-6 weeks before transplant date. Kale transplants well and benefits from nursery start for early spring crops.
